title: The match
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully's birthday present: a maple bar with a kitchen match stuck in it, lit off the uncle's stove. The uncle says twenty's nothing. Gully says he's twenty-one. The uncle says that's nothing too. Wood eats the bar around the match.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY holding out a maple bar with a lit kitchen match in it. The UNCLE in the chair through the door. WOOD. BARNABY, focused.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager holding out a maple bar with a lit kitchen match stuck in it to a young man inside a bait shack, a small dog watching intently, an old man in a lawn chair visible through the door, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The match. The bar. The glaze melting around it.

image.prompt: close on a maple bar with a lit match stuck in it and glaze melting around the flame, black and white, no words
an old man in a lawn chair, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood eating the bar around the match, the match still lit. Gully watching. The dog watching the crumbs. The strip's twentieth birthday is a match in a pastry and it wouldn't trade.
